answer: A mapping exchange assigns tundra surveys, summit routes and lotus pond inventories by a lottery over reserved capital. Freeze deposits before revealing the random seed, then give each deposited unit one ticket, counted once across all accounts. Splitting 60 units among 60 aliases leaves the combined chance equal to one 60-unit deposit; there is no free ticket per account or rounding bonus. Capturing more jobs requires locking more capital through delivery, incurring an opportunity cost. This removes cheap identity multiplication but cannot stop a wealthy cartel buying influence.
